newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bahn board may name new chief Monday.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bahn board may name new chief Monday.

text.p: German state railway Deutsche Bahn AG said on Monday it might name a new chief executive later in the day, although it neither confirmed nor denied reports the post would go to a government economics official.

Spokeswoman Anfried Baier-Fuchs declined to comment on reports that Johannes Ludewig, state secretary in the German Economics Ministry, would take over the group after Heinz Duerr moves to the supervisory board in July.
But she told Reuters the supervisory board presidium might issue a news release after a meeting on Monday night. The board was reportedly meeting to discuss a successor to Duerr.
"The presidium will meet tonight and may have news after the meeting," Baier-Fuchs said.

She also said the government was allowed to play a role in choosing a new chief for the state-owned rail system. "As the owner of Deutsche Bahn, the government can make suggestions to the supervisory board," Baier-Fuchs said.
Ludewig, a close ally of Chancellor Helmut Kohl, has served in the Economics Ministry and the Chancellor's office since 1975, including a stint as Kohl's coordinator for east Germany.
The opposition Social Democrats said naming Ludewig to head Deutsche Bahn would hinder the railway's conversion from a state bureaucracty to an independent corporation.
The Platow-Brief newsletter reported over the weekend that Ludewig had been named Duerr's successor.
